turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_process_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2 temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3 temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3
    cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1 temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 2 time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3
    time, Secondary treatment step 4 temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure
    temperature, Thermal exposure time) and `target` (the measured yield strength
    at room temperature (MPa)).
  - b3_htsteel_process_pool.csv: 34 CANDIDATE samples whose yield strength
    at room temperature (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield
strength at room temperature (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from
the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The pool consists exclusively of ~13Cr/~0.2C martensitic grades whose strength is controlled by carbon in solution and by tempering. Training examples of the same family show a clear inverse relationship between HT-stage-2 temperature and room-temperature yield strength (e.g. 250 °C temper on 0.12 C gives 930 MPa while 540 °C on the identical alloy gives only 780 MPa; 200 °C on a 0.075 C grade gives 990 MPa while 550 °C gives 760 MPa). Secondary-hardening peaks are absent in these low-alloy 13Cr steels, so the ranking is monotonic with tempering temperature.

Consequently the six candidates that receive a low-temperature temper and no subsequent aging stand far above the rest of the pool:

- 200 °C: c015 (0.205 C, no Ti) and c021 (0.20 C + 0.2 Ti)
- 300 °C: c018 (0.205 C, no Ti) and c017 (0.20 C + 0.2 Ti)
- 450 °C: c014 (0.205 C, no Ti) and c006 (0.20 C + 0.2 Ti)

Within each temperature the Ti-free, slightly higher-carbon variant is preferred: undissolved TiC would otherwise sequester carbon, and the extra 0.005 C plus the absence of Ni (an austenite stabilizer) both raise as-quenched martensite strength. The 50–150 °C gaps between the three tempering temperatures exceed any plausible composition effect, producing the order

c015 > c021 > c018 > c017 > c014.

(The remaining 28 candidates are tempered at 500–740 °C or receive an additional high-temperature age and are therefore predicted to lie 300–800 MPa lower.)

Final: c015, c021, c018, c017, c014
